title: Apply for the electric vehicle purchase rebate (individuals)
summary: Find out if you are eligible for and how to apply for a $3,000 cash rebate for purchasing a new electric or hydrogen vehicle in NSW.
intro:
If you have bought a new battery electric vehicle (BEV) or hydrogen fuel cell electric vehicle (FCEV) for personal use in NSW, you may be eligible for a $3,000 cash rebate.

Check full eligibility before applying.

One rebate is available per applicant.
who_can_apply: Must have bought a new BEV or FCEV for personal use in NSW.
Must have bought the car or paid a deposit by 31 December 2023.
Must have registered the vehicle for personal use in NSW on or after 1 September 2021.
The total cost must be less than $68,750 (including delivery costs, dealer fees, and accessories).
Must not have claimed a rebate for the vehicle in another state or territory.
The vehicle must not be registered before 1 September 2021.
The vehicle must not have been bought on or after 1 January 2024.

The vehicle must not be a leased vehicle, second-hand BEV or FCEV, grey import, hybrid electric vehicle, plug in hybrid electric vehicle, heavy truck, motorcycle, trailer, caravan, aeroplane, or boat.
what_you_need: A Revenue NSW electric vehicle portal account (you can sign up when applying).
Your Transport for NSW customer number.
A copy of a current and valid NSW Driver Licence.
A contract to purchase with the sales price and date of purchase or deposit payment.
Deposit receipt dated on or before 31 December 2023 (if applicable).
Tax invoice (if it is an interstate purchase or purchase from Tesla, Polestar and Vyro).

how_to_steps.text: Log in, or sign up to the Revenue NSW electric vehicle portal account.
Follow the prompts to complete the form.

more_info.text: Vehicles eligible for a rebate are also eligible for a stamp duty exemption.

faqs.q: How much is the rebate for buying an electric vehicle?
faqs.a: You may be eligible for a $3,000 cash rebate.

faqs.q: Who can apply for the rebate?
faqs.a: The rebate is for individuals who bought a new battery electric vehicle (BEV) or hydrogen fuel cell electric vehicle (FCEV) for personal use in NSW.

faqs.q: What is the maximum price limit for the vehicle?
faqs.a: The vehicle must have cost less than $68,750, including delivery costs, dealer fees, and accessories.
